title: AI Terms Classifier
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Place eight example systems in the narrowest of six nested categories, from Not AI to AI agent.

learningObjectives: The learner will classify eight example systems into the narrowest of six categories (Not AI, AI without machine learning, Machine learning, Generative AI, Large language model, AI agent), correctly placing at least seven of eight on the first attempt.
prerequisites: The terms artificial intelligence, machine learning, generative AI, large language model, and AI agent, from the section "A Ladder of Terms" in Chapter 4.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classify examples into nested categories with immediate feedback
keyQuestions: What defining feature does this system have?
What is the narrowest category whose definition it meets?
commonMisconceptions: Any software that feels smart is AI
A chatbot and an agent are the same thing
assessmentOpportunities: A thermostat switches the heat on below 68°F. Which category?
A 1990s chess program uses rules its programmers wrote. Which category?
A tool turns text into new spoken audio. Why is it not a large language model?
What makes a system an AI agent rather than a chatbot?

controls.name: Nested regions
controls.description: click a region to select it and read its definition. The innermost region you click is the one selected.

controls.name: Submit
controls.description: commits your choice. Two attempts per example; only the first counts.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: moves to the next example; after the eighth it shows your score.

controls.name: Try again
controls.description: reshuffles the examples and starts over.
